recipes.name: Keon's Slow Cooker Curry Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup
1 packet dry onion soup mix (such as Knorr® French Onion Soup Mix)
3 tablespoons curry powder, or to taste
2 teaspoons ground cayenne pepper, or to taste
3 large skinless, boneless chicken breast halves -- trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces

steps.text: Heat butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir onion in hot butter until browned, 5 to 10 minutes. Set aside.

Stir together coconut milk, condensed soups, dry soup mix, curry powder, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper in a large bowl until thoroughly combined. Place chicken into the bottom of the slow cooker and pour soup mixture over chicken. Stir in cooked onion, mushrooms, and peas until incorporated.
Cook on High for 1 hour and 30 minutes. Reduce heat to Low and cook for an additional 1 hour and 30 minutes to 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Keon's Slow Cooker Curry Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Chunks of chicken breast simmer in a creamy, curry-flavored sauce with coconut milk, peas, and mushrooms for a spicy take on a slow cooker dish.

review.reviewBody: I'm Keon (the creator of this recipe). Glad to see so many people enjoying it! I'm from Texas and like SPICY dishes, so you may want to tone down the cayenne if you don't like spicy as much as I do. Also, to reduce the sodium, you can use the low sodium soups. Enjoy!

Very good and so easy to make. I used olive oil instead of butter and browned the onion in the slow cooker on the "brown" setting, added the chicken toward the end of the browning b/c 3 hours on low - my slow cooker doesn't have a high and low setting - didn't seem enough to me. I used thinly sliced chicken breast cut into about 1" pieces so it cooked up nicely - was tender and delicious in the end product. I added some fresh baby spinach with about 30 minutes left to cook since I had some from the garden that needed to get used and it went very well. I also used 1/2 tsp of cayenne and can't imagine using more. It would have been too hot, especially since I am serving children along with adults. I'm curious about the serving size and calories though. What size serving is getting the 635 calorie mark? 2 cups or only 1? It seems like a lot for 1 cup but maybe the soups bumped it up.

Great base recipe. 2 cans of soup is a ton of calories and makes a ton of sauce. I used 1 can, 1/2 onion, 1TBL each Curry and Graham Masala, and 7 chicken breasts. I put chicken breasts into slow cooker whole and *FROZEN* Cooked mostly on low all day. Chicken was perfect, super moist, yummy, and falling apart.

Curry is not an exact science! My Indian acquaintances tell me it is "more like guidelines." Keeping that in mind and after reading a bunch of reviews, I did change a few things. I added a whole pound of mushrooms, omitted peas but added 1/2 pound baby spinach, added 3 carrots, omitted cayenne. I had yellow curry paste on hand and used that for the curry (3 Tbls). I served it with rice, sour cream and hot stuff of choice (sri racha, pepper flakes, sambal). All 6 of my eclectic eaters thought this was a great meal with a good balance of flavors & textures. We will make it again.

Very tasty. I was too lazy to saute the onions so threw them straight into the crockpot. I also added potatoes and carrots to make it more hearty. Even with these additions, it still had lots and lots of extra sauce. Next time I'll throw in even more veggies. Didn't have cayenne so used Franks Redhot Sauce. Perfect amount of heat. From other reviews, I'm glad I didn't add the cayenne as I'm sure it would have been too spicey for my tastebuds. I cooked on low for a longer period.. Easy and tasty. I'll definitely make again.

This came out surprisingly nice. I did it basically as in the recipe but rolled my chicken in curry powder and braised it in oil. I added garlic and ginger to the onion and added a cinnamon stick. I also added carrots for color.

I made this recipe tonight because my husband loves curry but it's never spicy enough when we dine out. 
I made this recipe by stove top and it was perfect. (I also added potatoes) 
I boiled my potatoes while I sauteéd the chicken. Mixed the other ingredients together in a separate bowl, then added everything to a pot to allow the flavors to combine. 20 minutes later, I served it over rice and my husband said it tasted better than any restaurant.

WOW. Just wow. I needed to use up some boneless thighs/breasts I had in the fridge, along with a ton of mushrooms. My family LOVES curry chicken, but I didn't have my usual ingredients on hand, which led me to THIS amazing recipe. I had to make a few changes due to lack of ingredients: I used 2 cans of cream of mushrooms (didn't have cream of chicken), beefy onion mix (as opposed to the regular french onion soup mix), and that was it. I read that this recipe was even better the next day, so I let it sit overnight before trying. I did note that the sauce was a bit spicy (not even close to too spicy for me, but I have to be careful of my husband's sensitive palette or he won't eat it) so I added in about a cup of light sour cream - PERFECTION. This dish was not only suitable for my husband, but also our 2 yr old - she does have a bit of a refined palette and doesn't mind spicy things, but without the sour cream I believe it would have been too spicy for each of them - but again, perfectly fine for me! I may just mix in the sour cream to their servings in the future, since i only added it at the very end of warming it back up. I just had it again today for lunch and MY GOODNESS it's just unbelievable. I cannot wait to make it again and again!!! Thank you, Keon.

This is so good! The original recipe has way too much sodium though so I used Campbells healthy request, low sodium salt, low or no sodium added peas. It has a really good heat to it with 2 tsp of cayenne. At first I thought it might be way too spicy but its a good spicy. I used chicken breast cut into 2" chunks but it would probably be good with any type of bone-in chicken. Great recipe!

1/2 to 1 tsp of cayenne is plenty. Great flavour. Didn’t have coconut milk, so used regular milk, with some coconut oil.
Mixed everything together in the crockpot.

This recipe was SO EASY to make and awesome! I only gave it a 4 star because of the cayenne pepper. I should have listened to the reviews and used less but I am a Trini and thought I could handle the pepper. I could handle it but to me it took away the curry taste and all you tasted was spicy. Everyone still loved it and wanted seconds though, but that is my advice(lessen the cayenne). I also didn't stick to the recipe. Every recipe can be tweaked. That is why it was so easy. I used chicken breasts, less sodium soup, and a bag of frozen mixed veggies. I mixed everything in the crock pot and omitted the salt and black pepper. All the other ingredients give it enough salt and pepper! Once everything was thoroughly mixed, I added the chicken breasts and browned onions and frozen veggies. Then I cooked it and served with rice. Thank you Keon for this recipe! It was great!

I've made it a few times now. I always add extra curry and cayenne because we like it a bit spicier. This last time round, we had to replace the onion soup mix with canned. It turned out thinner but still quite delicious!
Could have put more curry in or a hotter one , but was totally enjoyable

I made this recipe exactly as directed except that I cut the cayenne pepper to one tsp, My husband liked it, but it just didn't appeal very much to me. I don't know why. I love spice and curry and just about all East Indian offerings. It just seemed a bit to heavy for me. I won't be making this again. Sorry Keon.
Wow. What a delicious recipe. I did cut the curry back to 1 1/2 tablespoons as it was all I had on hand. Plenty spicy for us. Hubby loved this dish .
followed the recipe to the tee my husband said it may be his new favorite meal, I will definitely make this again
Stayed with the recipe except reduced cayenne to 1 teaspoon and added a bit more curry. Left out the added salt. It was really good. I will make this again.
Yes I made it on the stove and added more curry. Loved it am making it again.
My family loved it! I will definitely make this again.

Made the recipe exactly as listed, except only put 2 tbsp of curry --- turned out great! Might reduce the amount of coconut milk slightly as it was a little runny, but otherwise no complaints. Definitely a recipe for those who like heat/spice with their meal!
